question: What is the percentage composition of the element of H2SO3?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.5% H, 39% S, 58.5% O.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sulfurous acid (H2SO3) has the molecular formula H2SO3, with a molar mass of 82 g/mol (H = 2 × 1 = 2, S = 32, O = 3 × 16 = 48). (सल्फ्यूरस अम्ल — 2.5% H, 39% S, 58.5% O)

 

• % of Hydrogen = (2/82) × 100 = 2.44% ≈ 2.5%.

 

• % of Sulphur = (32/82) × 100 = 39.02% ≈ 39%.

 

• % of Oxygen = (48/82) × 100 = 58.53% ≈ 58.5%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• For comparison, sulfuric acid (H2SO4), molar mass 98 g/mol, has the approximate composition 2.04% H, 32.65% S, 65.31% O.

 

• Sulfurous acid is a weak, unstable diprotic acid formed when sulphur dioxide (SO2) dissolves in water; it is used as a reducing agent and bleaching agent.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (2.5% H, 58.5% S, 39% O): The percentages for sulphur and oxygen are interchanged; it is oxygen, not sulphur, that makes up 58.5%.

 

• Option 2 (33% H, 16% S, 51% O): These values do not correspond to the actual molar composition of H2SO3 at all.

 

• Option 3 (58.5% H, 39% S, 2.5% O): The percentages for hydrogen and oxygen are interchanged; hydrogen is the smallest share (2.5%), not oxygen.

question: Which is the correct sequence of lakes according to depth (from maximum to minimum) ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Baikal > Tanganyika > Caspian Sea > Vostok.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lake Baikal in Russia is the deepest lake in the world, with a maximum depth of about 1,642 metres; it is also the world's largest freshwater lake by volume. (सबसे गहरी झील — बैकाल झील)

 

• Lake Tanganyika in East Africa is the second deepest lake, with a maximum depth of about 1,470 metres, and is also the world's second-largest freshwater lake by volume.

 

• The Caspian Sea, the world's largest inland water body, has a maximum depth of about 1,025 metres, ranking it third among the deepest lakes.

 

• Lake Vostok, a subglacial lake buried under the Antarctic ice sheet, is comparatively much shallower than the above three, placing it last in this sequence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lake Baikal holds roughly one-fifth of the world's unfrozen freshwater and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

 

• Lake Vostok is notable as the largest of Antarctica's subglacial lakes, discovered beneath about 4 km of ice.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Caspian Sea > Tanganyika > Vostok > Baikal): Wrongly places the Caspian Sea first and Baikal last, the exact reverse of the actual order.

 

• Option 2 (Baikal > Caspian Sea > Tanganyika > Vostok): Wrongly places the Caspian Sea ahead of Tanganyika, though Tanganyika is deeper than the Caspian Sea.

 

• Option 4 (Caspian Sea > Baikal > Tanganyika > Vostok): Wrongly places the Caspian Sea first, whereas it is actually the third deepest of the four.

question: Justice NV Ramana was appointed as the ___________ Chief Justice of India in April 2021.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 48th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Justice Nuthalapati Venkata Ramana (N.V. Ramana) was sworn in as the 48th Chief Justice of India (CJI) on 24 April 2021. (भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश — जस्टिस एन.वी. रमना, 48वें)

 

• He succeeded Chief Justice S.A. Bobde and served as CJI until his retirement on 26 August 2021, after which Justice U.U. Lalit became the 49th CJI.

 

• Justice Ramana hailed from Andhra Pradesh and was also known for championing free legal aid and expanding e-courts infrastructure during his tenure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Chief Justice of India is appointed by the President of India under Article 124 of the Constitution, conventionally on the basis of seniority.

 

• Justice D.Y. Chandrachud later became the 50th CJI in November 2022.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (47th): This was the position of the preceding CJI, S.A. Bobde, not N.V. Ramana.

 

• Option 3 (46th): This corresponds to a CJI from an earlier period, not N.V. Ramana.

 

• Option 4 (44th): This corresponds to a CJI from an earlier period, not N.V. Ramana.

question: In a plant, ________ is present in the middle lamella, primary cell and secondary walls and accumulates in the initial stages of development during cell expansion.
solution_text:
The correct answer is pectin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pectin is a complex polysaccharide found abundantly in the middle lamella (the layer that cements adjacent plant cells together) as well as in the primary and secondary cell walls. (पेक्टिन — मध्य पटलिका/कोशिका भित्ति)

 

• It accumulates in the early stages of cell wall development, especially during cell expansion and growth, giving the wall flexibility.

 

• Pectin is a major component responsible for cell-to-cell adhesion, wall porosity, and it also plays a role in plant defence and fruit firmness/ripening.

 

• Commercially, pectin extracted from fruits (like citrus peels and apples) is widely used as a gelling agent in jams and jellies.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Plant primary cell walls are mainly composed of cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin, whereas secondary walls additionally contain lignin.

 

• The middle lamella is rich in calcium pectate, which binds neighbouring cells together.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (chitin): Chitin is a structural polysaccharide found in fungal cell walls and the exoskeleton of arthropods, not in plant cell walls.

 

• Option 2 (gelatin): Gelatin is an animal-derived protein obtained from collagen; it has no role in plant cell wall structure.

 

• Option 3 (alginate): Alginate is a polysaccharide extracted from brown algae (seaweed), not a component of higher-plant cell walls.

question: Which of the following was established on the recommendation of the Hilton Young Commission?
solution_text:
The correct answer is RBI.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was established following the recommendations of the Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance (1926), popularly known as the Hilton Young Commission. (हिल्टन यंग आयोग — भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक)

 

• The RBI was set up under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and commenced operations on 1 April 1935, as India's central bank.

 

• It was originally established as a shareholders' bank and was nationalised in 1949, after independence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Hilton Young Commission was headed by Edward Hilton Young and was set up to examine India's currency and banking system.

 

• The first Governor of the RBI was Sir Osborne Smith, and the first Indian Governor was C.D. Deshmukh.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (SEBI): The Securities and Exchange Board of India was set up in 1988 and given statutory powers in 1992, to regulate the securities market.

 

• Option 3 (SBI): The State Bank of India traces its origin to the Imperial Bank of India (1921) and was renamed/reconstituted as SBI in 1955.

 

• Option 4 (NABARD): The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development was established in 1982 on the recommendation of the Shivaraman Committee.

question: The Olympic Games are held every ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is fourth year.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Olympic Games (both Summer and Winter) are held once every four years, a period known as an Olympiad. (ओलंपिक खेल — प्रत्येक चौथे वर्ष)

 

• The modern Olympic Games were revived by Baron Pierre de Coubertin, and the first modern edition was held in Athens, Greece, in 1896.

 

• Since 1994, the Summer and Winter Olympics have been staggered so that each is still held every four years but two years apart from each other.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Olympic Games are organised by the International Olympic Committee (IOC), headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland.

 

• The 2024 Summer Olympics were held in Paris, France.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (fifth year): Incorrect; the Olympics are not held on a five-year cycle.

 

• Option 2 (third year): Incorrect; the Olympics are not held on a three-year cycle.

 

• Option 4 (second year): Incorrect; a two-year cycle instead describes the gap between the Summer and Winter Games, not the interval of each individually.

question: Joravarsinh Jadav was awarded the Padma Shri 2019 for his contribution to which of the following dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarati folk dance form, Bhavai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Joravarsinh Jadav was a noted Gujarati folklorist honoured with the Padma Shri in 2019 for his lifelong contribution to Gujarat's folk arts and folk theatre, particularly the traditional dance-drama form Bhavai. (भवाई — गुजराती लोक नृत्य)

 

• He authored over 90 works on Gujarati folk culture, folklore and folk literature, and worked to document and preserve endangered folk art forms.

 

• He founded the Gujarat Lok Kala Foundation to promote and popularise folk artists through mass media, including television and radio.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhavai is a traditional folk theatre form of Gujarat, combining dance, music, and dialogue, traditionally performed at night in front of temples.

 

• The Padma Shri is India's fourth-highest civilian award, conferred for distinguished contribution in various fields, including art.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Karnataka folk dance, Yakshagana): Yakshagana is a traditional dance-drama of coastal Karnataka, unrelated to Joravarsinh Jadav.

 

• Option 3 (Maharashtrian folk dance form, Tamasha): Tamasha is a folk theatre form of Maharashtra, unrelated to Joravarsinh Jadav.

 

• Option 4 (Rajasthani folk dance form, Ghoomar): Ghoomar is a traditional folk dance of Rajasthan, unrelated to Joravarsinh Jadav.

question: 'Hind Swaraj' or 'Indian Home Rule' is written by which of the following freedom fighters?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Hind Swaraj' (Indian Home Rule) was written by Mahatma Gandhi in 1909, originally in Gujarati aboard the ship Kildonan Castle while returning from London to South Africa. (हिंद स्वराज — महात्मा गांधी)

 

• In the book, Gandhi critiques modern Western civilisation, railways, lawyers and doctors, and lays out his vision of true self-rule (Swaraj) based on non-violence and self-discipline.

 

• The book was subsequently banned by the British Government in India for its politically radical views, but Gandhi later brought out an English translation himself.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi's other major writings include his autobiography 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth'.

 

• Gandhi returned to India permanently from South Africa in January 1915.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Dadabhai Naoroji): He is known for the 'Drain of Wealth' theory, presented in his book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'.

 

• Option 3 (Bal Gangadhar Tilak): He authored 'Gita Rahasya' while imprisoned in Mandalay, not Hind Swaraj.

 

• Option 4 (Annie Besant): She was a theosophist and Home Rule Movement leader but did not author Hind Swaraj.

question: Who among the following won the Padma award for the year 2023 for his efforts on S &T based innovative ways of creating Naga folk music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Moa Subong.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Moa Subong, a musician and instrument innovator from Nagaland, was conferred the Padma Shri in 2023 for his science-and-technology-based innovative contribution to reviving and creating Naga folk music. (मोआ सुबोंग — नागा लोक संगीत)

 

• Along with his wife Arenla, a folk-music educator, he studied the tonal limitations of traditional Naga instruments and developed the 'Bamhum', a bamboo wind instrument, to overcome them.

 

• He also founded the folk-fusion band Abiogenesis, which promotes Naga folk music using his innovative instruments.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Padma Shri, India's fourth-highest civilian award, is given across categories including art, social work, public affairs, science and engineering.

 

• Other grassroots innovators have similarly been honoured with the Padma Shri for S&T-based revival of traditional Indian art forms.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (CV Raju): Not associated with the 2023 Padma award for Naga folk music innovation.

 

• Option 3 (Baba Balia): Not associated with the 2023 Padma award for Naga folk music innovation.

 

• Option 4 (T Senka Ao): Not associated with the 2023 Padma award for Naga folk music innovation.

question: The total number of medals won by India in Paralympic 2020 was:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 19.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the Tokyo 2020 Paralympic Games (held in 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic), India won a total of 19 medals — its best-ever Paralympic performance at the time. (पैरालंपिक 2020 — भारत के 19 पदक)

 

• The medal tally comprised 5 gold, 8 silver and 6 bronze medals.

 

• Notable gold medallists included Avani Lekhara (shooting, India's first woman to win a Paralympic gold), Sumit Antil, Manish Narwal, Pramod Bhagat and Krishna Nagar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's medal tally more than tripled compared to the Rio 2016 Paralympics, where it had won 4 medals.

 

• India further improved on this performance at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, winning 29 medals.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (8): This corresponds only to the number of silver medals won, not the total.

 

• Option 2 (6): This corresponds only to the number of bronze medals won, not the total.

 

• Option 3 (5): This corresponds only to the number of gold medals won, not the total.

question: "Amatya" in the Saptang Theory of Kautilya denotes which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Minister and Officials.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kautilya's Saptanga theory of state, described in the Arthashastra, identifies seven organic elements (Prakritis) of a state, of which 'Amatya' refers to the ministers and officials/bureaucracy who assist the king in administration. (सप्तांग सिद्धांत — अमात्य: मंत्री एवं अधिकारी)

 

• The seven limbs of the Saptanga are: Swami (king), Amatya (ministers), Janapada (territory/population), Durga (fort), Kosha (treasury), Danda (army/coercive power) and Mitra (ally/friend).

 

• The Amatya was expected to be well-versed in various sciences, loyal, and capable of assisting the king in governance and policy-making.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kautilya (also known as Chanakya or Vishnugupta) was the chief advisor to Chandragupta Maurya and author of the Arthashastra, a treatise on statecraft, economics and military strategy.

 

• The Saptanga theory is often compared to a human body, where each limb must function well for the state to remain healthy.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Friend): This corresponds to 'Mitra', another of the seven limbs, not Amatya.

 

• Option 3 (Fort): This corresponds to 'Durga', another of the seven limbs, not Amatya.

 

• Option 4 (Territory): This corresponds to 'Janapada', another of the seven limbs, not Amatya.

question: Which five-year plan emphasised on the development of industries and industrial base in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Second.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61) was based on the Mahalanobis Model, formulated by economist P.C. Mahalanobis, and laid special emphasis on the rapid development of heavy and basic industries. (द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना — औद्योगीकरण पर बल)

 

• It aimed to build a strong industrial base, promoting public-sector enterprises in steel, machinery and capital goods production.

 

• Major public-sector steel plants like Bhilai, Rourkela and Durgapur were set up during this plan period.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model and gave priority to agriculture.

 

• The Third Five-Year Plan (1961-66) aimed for a self-reliant and self-generating economy but was disrupted by the 1962 and 1965 wars and successive droughts.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (Fourth): The Fourth Plan (1969-74) focused on the twin objectives of growth with stability and progress towards self-reliance, not primarily heavy industry.

 

• Option 3 (Third): The Third Plan aimed for a self-reliant economy but is not primarily remembered for industrial emphasis; that distinction belongs to the Second Plan.

 

• Option 4 (First): The First Plan focused chiefly on agriculture and irrigation, not industry.

question: In which city of Assam is the Tea Festival celebrated every year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jorhat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Assam Tea Festival is celebrated annually in Jorhat, often called the 'Tea City of India', since it lies at the heart of Assam's tea-growing region. (असम चाय महोत्सव — जोरहाट)

 

• The festival showcases Assam's rich tea heritage through tea garden visits, tea tasting, cultural performances and stalls of Assamese cuisine and handicrafts.

 

• Jorhat is home to numerous historic tea estates and the Tocklai Tea Research Institute, one of the oldest tea research stations in the world.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Assam is India's largest tea-producing state and is known for its distinctive malty, full-bodied CTC and orthodox black teas.

 

• Assam's tea industry was pioneered in the 19th century following the discovery of indigenous tea plants by Robert Bruce in the region.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Guwahati): Guwahati is Assam's largest city and gateway to the Northeast, but the Tea Festival is centred at Jorhat.

 

• Option 2 (Silchar): Silchar is a major city in the Barak Valley, not the venue of the Assam Tea Festival.

 

• Option 4 (Dibrugarh): Dibrugarh is another major tea-hub city of Assam, but the annual Tea Festival is specifically identified with Jorhat.

question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pteridophyta – Cycas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Cycas is a gymnosperm, not a pteridophyte, so the pairing 'Pteridophyta – Cycas' is incorrect. (साइकस — जिम्नोस्पर्म, टेरिडोफाइटा नहीं)

 

• Pteridophyta (vascular cryptogams) is correctly represented by examples like ferns (e.g., Pteris, Dryopteris), Selaginella, Equisetum and Marsilea.

 

• Gymnosperms, meaning 'naked-seeded' plants, include examples such as Cycas, Pinus, Cedrus and Gnetum, all of which bear seeds not enclosed in an ovary/fruit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The plant kingdom is broadly classified into Thallophyta, Bryophyta, Pteridophyta, Gymnosperms and Angiosperms, based on the presence of vascular tissue, seeds and flowers.

 

• Bryophytes (e.g., mosses, liverworts) are called the 'amphibians of the plant kingdom' as they need water for fertilisation.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Bryophyta – Moss): This pairing is correct; moss (e.g., Funaria) is a classic example of Bryophyta.

 

• Option 2 (Angiosperms – Rose): This pairing is correct; rose is a well-known flowering plant (Angiosperm).

 

• Option 4 (Gymnosperms – Pinus): This pairing is correct; Pinus (pine) is a classic example of a Gymnosperm.

question: India can be considered to be a country with Demographic Dividend due to ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is high population between 15-64 years.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Demographic Dividend refers to the economic growth potential arising from a high proportion of the working-age population (15-64 years) relative to the non-working-age population (children and elderly). (जनसांख्यिकीय लाभांश — कार्यशील आयु वर्ग 15-64 वर्ष)

 

• India is currently experiencing this dividend as more than 60% of its population falls in the working-age bracket, offering a large potential labour force to boost productivity and savings.

 

• This window of opportunity is temporary and depends on the country's ability to provide adequate education, skill development, and employment to this working-age population.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's demographic dividend is projected to last until around 2055-56, as per various demographic studies.

 

• The concept was popularised in development economics to explain the East Asian economic boom, driven by a similarly favourable age structure.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (high population above 70 years): A high elderly population represents an ageing burden, the opposite of a demographic dividend.

 

• Option 3 (high population between 10-20 years): This is only a part of the pre-working-age/young population, not the full working-age bracket that defines the dividend.

 

• Option 4 (high total population): A high total population alone (without a favourable age structure) does not by itself constitute a demographic dividend.

question: The famous musician, Faiyaz Khan is associated with which musical instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tabla.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Faiyaz Khan (1934-2014), belonging to the Delhi Gharana, was internationally renowned as a tabla maestro. (फैयाज़ खान — तबला वादक)

 

• Born in Sikar, Rajasthan, into a family of musicians, he came from a lineage where his father Nazir Khan was a sarangi and tabla player at the court of the Maharaja of Karauli.

 

• He performed and taught extensively, contributing significantly to the Delhi Gharana style of tabla playing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has several distinct tabla gharanas, including Delhi, Ajrada, Lucknow, Farukhabad, Benares and Punjab.

 

• A separate, differently-spelt vocalist, Ustad Faiyaz Khan of the Kirana/Agra Gharana, is known for Hindustani classical vocal music, but the tabla maestro is the artist referenced here.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Shehnai): The shehnai is most famously associated with Ustad Bismillah Khan, not Faiyaz Khan.

 

• Option 2 (Veena): The veena is a stringed instrument associated with artists like S. Balachander, not Faiyaz Khan.

 

• Option 4 (Sitar): The sitar is most famously associated with artists like Pandit Ravi Shankar, not Faiyaz Khan.

question: The Raigarh Gharana is associated with which of the following dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Raigarh Gharana is one of the important schools (gharanas) of the classical dance form Kathak, developed under the patronage of the princely state of Raigarh (in present-day Chhattisgarh). (रायगढ़ घराना — कथक नृत्य)

 

• It flourished notably under Raja Chakradhar Singh, a great patron of arts, who himself was a skilled Kathak dancer, tabla player and musician.

 

• The Raigarh Gharana is particularly known for its emphasis on rhythmic (tal) work and intricate footwork, blending elements from other Kathak gharanas like Jaipur and Lucknow.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The three major traditional gharanas of Kathak are Jaipur, Lucknow and Banaras; Raigarh emerged as a significant later centre.

 

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, traditionally associated with storytelling through rhythmic footwork and expressive gestures.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Odissi): Odissi is a classical dance form of Odisha, unrelated to the Raigarh Gharana.

 

• Option 2 (Kathakali): Kathakali is a classical dance-drama form of Kerala, unrelated to the Raigarh Gharana.

 

• Option 4 (Manipuri): Manipuri is a classical dance form of Manipur, unrelated to the Raigarh Gharana.

question: Whose law states that total energy per unit mass of flowing fluid, at any point in the subsurface, is the sum of the kinetic, potential, and fluid-pressure energy and is equal to a constant value?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Daniel Bernoulli.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bernoulli's Principle, formulated by the Swiss mathematician Daniel Bernoulli, states that the total energy of a flowing fluid (comprising kinetic energy, potential energy, and pressure energy) at any point remains constant along a streamline, for an ideal, incompressible, non-viscous fluid. (बर्नौली सिद्धांत — डेनियल बर्नौली)

 

• It is mathematically expressed as: P + ½ρv² + ρgh = constant, where P is pressure energy, ½ρv² is kinetic energy, and ρgh is potential energy per unit volume.

 

• This principle explains phenomena such as the lift generated on an aircraft wing and the working of a carburettor and atomizer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bernoulli's principle is a direct consequence of the law of conservation of energy applied to fluid flow.

 

• It was published in Daniel Bernoulli's book 'Hydrodynamica' (1738).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (Evangelista Torricelli): Torricelli is known for Torricelli's Law (efflux speed of a fluid from an orifice) and for inventing the mercury barometer.

 

• Option 3 (Blaise Pascal): Pascal is known for Pascal's Law, which relates to the transmission of pressure in an enclosed fluid.

 

• Option 4 (Marie Poiseuille): Poiseuille is known for Poiseuille's Law, describing the laminar flow of viscous fluid through a narrow tube.

question: What is the name of the flagship program that was launched in 2005 to address the lack of infrastructure in urban India?
option_2: Integrated Development of Small & Medium Towns
option_3: Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation
option_4: Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) was launched by the Government of India on 3 December 2005 as its flagship programme to improve urban infrastructure and basic services in Indian cities. (जवाहरलाल नेहरू राष्ट्रीय शहरी नवीकरण मिशन — 2005)

 

• It covered 65 mission cities and had two major sub-missions: Urban Infrastructure and Governance (UIG) and Basic Services to the Urban Poor (BSUP).

 

• The mission aimed to ensure planned development, improved connectivity, sanitation, and housing for the urban poor over a seven-year period (later extended).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• JNNURM was succeeded by the Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT), launched in 2015.

 

• Other urban missions launched later include the Smart Cities Mission (2015) and Swachh Bharat Mission - Urban (2014).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (National Urban Livelihoods Mission): Launched in 2013, it focuses on urban poverty alleviation through skill development and self-employment, not infrastructure.

 

• Option 2 (Integrated Development of Small & Medium Towns): This was an earlier, smaller-scale urban development scheme, not the 2005 flagship programme.

 

• Option 3 (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation): AMRUT was launched in 2015, replacing JNNURM, not in 2005.

question: The Indian Constitution was enacted on which of the following dates?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 26th November 1949.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Constituent Assembly of India adopted and enacted the Constitution of India on 26 November 1949, a date now commemorated as 'Constitution Day' or 'Samvidhan Divas'. (संविधान दिवस — 26 नवंबर 1949)

 

• The Constitution came into full force/effect on 26 January 1950, a date chosen to commemorate the Purna Swaraj declaration of 1930; this day is celebrated as Republic Day.

 

• The Constituent Assembly took nearly 2 years, 11 months and 18 days to draft the Constitution, under the chairmanship of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as head of the Drafting Committee.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's Constitution is the longest written constitution in the world.

 

• The Constituent Assembly was chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad, who later became independent India's first President.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (26th January 1949): Incorrect date; the Constitution was neither adopted nor enforced on this date.

 

• Option 3 (26th November 1950): Incorrect date; the Constitution was adopted in 1949, not 1950.

 

• Option 4 (26th January 1950): This is the date the Constitution came into force (Republic Day), not the date it was enacted/adopted.

question: Which state is also known as the 'Molasses basin', which is made up of soft unconsolidated deposits?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mizoram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mizoram is also known as the 'Molasses Basin', since it largely comprises soft, unconsolidated Tertiary sedimentary rocks (molasse-type sediments) formed from erosion of the rising Himalayan/Indo-Burman ranges. (मोलेसिस बेसिन — मिजोरम)

 

• Geologically, Mizoram falls under the highly folded and faulted hill ranges of the Indo-Myanmar mobile belt, marked by parallel hill ranges running north-south.

 

• Because of these soft, loosely consolidated deposits, the region is prone to landslides and soil erosion.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mizoram's terrain consists mainly of north-south trending hill ranges separated by river valleys, with the Blue Mountain (Phawngpui) as its highest peak.

 

• The term 'molasse' in geology refers to soft sedimentary rocks (sandstone, shale, conglomerate) deposited in a foreland basin during mountain-building (orogeny).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (Manipur): Manipur is characterised by a central valley surrounded by hills but is not termed the 'Molasses Basin'.

 

• Option 3 (Nagaland): Nagaland has rugged hill terrain but is not specifically termed the 'Molasses Basin'.

 

• Option 4 (Meghalaya): Meghalaya is composed largely of older Precambrian rocks (Meghalaya Plateau/Shillong Plateau), not soft molasse-type deposits.

question: Abdur Razzaq, an envoy from Persia came to Vijaynagar during the reign of whose rule?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Deva Raya II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Abdur Razzaq, a Persian ambassador sent by the Timurid ruler Shah Rukh, visited the Vijayanagara Empire in 1443 CE, during the reign of Deva Raya II. (अब्दुर रज़्ज़ाक — देवराय द्वितीय के शासनकाल में विजयनगर यात्रा)

 

• In his travel account, Abdur Razzaq gave a vivid description of the city of Vijayanagara, praising its prosperity, markets, and the grandeur of the royal court.

 

• Deva Raya II (also called Prauda Deva Raya) is considered one of the greatest rulers of the Sangama dynasty, known for military reforms including recruitment of Muslim archers and expansion of the empire.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable foreign travellers to Vijayanagara include the Italian traveller Niccolò de' Conti (during Deva Raya I's reign) and the Portuguese travellers Domingo Paes and Fernão Nuniz (during Krishnadeva Raya's reign).

 

• The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 CE by Harihara I and Bukka I.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Bukka I): Bukka I was a co-founder of the Vijayanagara Empire, but Abdur Razzaq's visit occurred later, during Deva Raya II's reign.

 

• Option 2 (Harihar II): Harihara II ruled earlier (late 14th century) and was not the ruler during Abdur Razzaq's visit.

 

• Option 3 (Deva Raya I): It was the Italian traveller Niccolò de' Conti, not Abdur Razzaq, who visited during Deva Raya I's reign.

question: As per Article 172(2) ______________ of a State shall NOT be subject to dissolution.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Legislative Council.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Article 172(2) of the Indian Constitution, the Legislative Council of a State (Vidhan Parishad) is a permanent body and is NOT subject to dissolution, though one-third of its members retire every second year. (विधान परिषद — भंग नहीं होती)

 

• In contrast, the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) of a state has a normal term of five years and can be dissolved earlier, as governed by Article 172(1).

 

• The Legislative Council is analogous to the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) at the national level, which is likewise a permanent, continuing chamber.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• A state Legislative Council can be created or abolished by Parliament, under Article 169, upon a resolution passed by the concerned state's Legislative Assembly.

 

• As of now, only a few states — including Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh — have a Legislative Council (bicameral legislature).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Legislative Assembly): The Legislative Assembly of a state IS subject to dissolution (either on completion of its term or earlier), governed by Article 172(1).

 

• Option 3 (House of People): The Lok Sabha (House of the People) is the lower house of Parliament, not a state legislature, and it too is subject to dissolution.

 

• Option 4 (Council of States): The Rajya Sabha (Council of States) is the permanent upper house of Parliament, not a state body — Article 172 pertains to state legislatures.

question: Justice Indu Malhotra penned a dissenting opinion in which of the following landmark judgements?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Entry of women to Sabarimala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the Sabarimala Temple entry case (Indian Young Lawyers Association v. State of Kerala, 2018), Justice Indu Malhotra was the lone dissenting judge on the five-judge Constitution Bench, which by a 4:1 majority allowed the entry of women of all ages into the Sabarimala temple. (सबरीमाला मंदिर मामला — जस्टिस इंदु मल्होत्रा की असहमति)

 

• She held that matters of deep religious sentiment should not ordinarily be tested on the sole touchstone of Article 14 (equality), and that issues of religious practice, being a matter for the religious community, should not be decided by courts through the lens of rationality.

 

• Justice Indu Malhotra was also the first woman lawyer to be directly elevated to the Supreme Court of India as a judge (in 2018), without having served as a High Court judge beforehand.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sabarimala verdict was later referred to a larger nine-judge bench for reconsideration on broader questions of religious freedom.

 

• Justice Indu Malhotra retired from the Supreme Court in March 2021.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Basic structure doctrine): This doctrine was propounded in the landmark Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), long before Justice Malhotra's tenure.

 

• Option 2 (Preamble part of the Constitution): The question of whether the Preamble is part of the Constitution was also addressed in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), not one involving Justice Malhotra.

 

• Option 4 (Land reforms in India): Land reform cases (e.g., relating to Article 31 and the Ninth Schedule) were decided much earlier and are unrelated to Justice Indu Malhotra's tenure.

question: Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is January 1915.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mahatma Gandhi returned to India permanently from South Africa on 9 January 1915, landing at Bombay (Mumbai). (महात्मा गांधी की भारत वापसी — जनवरी 1915)

 

• This date is now commemorated annually as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (Non-Resident Indian Day), celebrating the contributions of the Indian diaspora.

 

• Before returning, Gandhi had spent about 21 years in South Africa (1893-1914), where he developed and practised his philosophy of Satyagraha (non-violent resistance) against racial discrimination.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• On the advice of his political mentor Gopal Krishna Gokhale, Gandhi spent his first year back in India travelling across the country to understand its people and conditions before joining active politics.

 

• Gandhi's first major public involvement in Indian politics came with the Champaran Satyagraha in Bihar (1917).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (January 1912): Incorrect; Gandhi was still in South Africa in 1912, actively involved in the Satyagraha movement there.

 

• Option 3 (January 1914): Incorrect; Gandhi left South Africa only in 1914 and reached India in January 1915, not January 1914.

 

• Option 4 (January 1913): Incorrect; Gandhi was still in South Africa in 1913, engaged in the Great March protest against discriminatory laws.
